lines.text: Mārcus canem magnum habet. Canis in hortō vīllae habitat.
lines.en: Marcus has a big dog. The dog lives in the villa's garden.

lines.text: Māne Mārcus ad scholam ambulat, et canis cum puerō currit.
lines.en: In the morning Marcus walks to school, and the dog runs with the boy.

lines.text: Sed canis in scholā nōn est grātus. Magister canem nōn amat!
lines.en: But the dog is not welcome at school. The teacher doesn't like the dog!

lines.text: Canis igitur ante portam sedet et discipulōs spectat.
lines.en: So the dog sits in front of the gate and watches the students.

lines.text: Post scholam Mārcus et canis per viās urbis ad vīllam currunt.
lines.en: After school Marcus and the dog run through the city streets to the villa.

lines.text: Iūlia rīdet: “Canis tuus discipulus bonus est; semper in scholā est!”
lines.en: Julia laughs: “Your dog is a good student; he's always at school!”

lines.text: Nocte canis sub mēnsā dormit, et Mārcus in lectō dormit.
lines.en: At night the dog sleeps under the table, and Marcus sleeps in bed.

lines.text: Galēnus medicus Graecus erat. Ōlim in oppidō Pergamō habitābat.
lines.en: Galen was a Greek doctor. Once he lived in the town of Pergamum.

lines.text: Prīmum gladiātōrēs cūrābat, quī saepe vulnera gravia habēbant.
lines.en: At first he treated gladiators, who often had serious wounds.

lines.text: Deinde Rōmam vēnit. Rōmae multōs aegrōs cūrāvit.
lines.en: Then he came to Rome. In Rome he treated many sick people.

lines.text: Galēnus dē corpore hominis multōs librōs scrīpsit.
lines.en: Galen wrote many books about the human body.

lines.text: Dīcēbat: sanguis in corpore est, et cor magnum est.
lines.en: He used to say: blood is in the body, and the heart is important.

lines.text: Medicī librōs eius per multōs annōs lēgērunt.
lines.en: Doctors read his books for many years.

lines.text: Hodiē quoque discipulī medicīnae nōmen Galēnī sciunt.
lines.en: Today too, medical students know Galen's name.
